title: IC Memo — Saltglass Photonics Series A (INVEST)
body:
NORDWIND VENTURES — INVESTMENT COMMITTEE MEMO

Company: Saltglass Photonics GmbH (Dresden)
Round: Series A — EUR 12M total; Nordwind to lead EUR 7M at EUR 38M pre-money
Prepared by: Jonas Berg (Associate)
Reviewed by: Maya Chen (Partner)
Date: 14 April 2026

RECOMMENDATION: INVEST

1. Summary
Saltglass Photonics builds tunable photonic filters for datacentre optical interconnects, cutting transceiver power draw by roughly 30% in customer pilots. Two design wins with tier-two European cloud operators are already generating EUR 1.4M ARR-equivalent in paid pilots, with conversion to volume orders expected in Q4 2026. We propose leading the Series A with a EUR 7M cheque and a board seat for Maya.

2. Team
The company was founded in 2023 by Dr. Ingrid Solheim (CEO), previously a group lead in integrated photonics at Helionix Labs in Trondheim, and Rafael Duarte (CTO), who ran packaging engineering at the same lab before spinning out. Ingrid has been the standout in our meetings: technically precise, honest about yield problems, and unusually good at translating physics into procurement language. Rafael holds the core patents (three granted, two pending) and has assembled a 14-person team with very low churn.

3. Market and competition
Optical interconnect spend is being pulled forward by AI cluster buildouts. The credible competitive set is small; the main risk is in-house development by hyperscalers, which the founders mitigate by focusing on the tier-two operators the giants ignore.

4. Diligence
We commissioned three expert calls. The most decisive was a 90-minute session on 2 April with Dr. Wei-Lin Zhao, formerly head of the photonics division at Helionix Labs and Ingrid's old boss, who described her as "the person I would least like to compete against" and independently confirmed the 30% power figure is conservative at scale. Full call notes are in the diligence folder. Customer references (both pilot operators) were strong on responsiveness; one flagged documentation gaps, which the company acknowledges.

5. Deal dynamics
This round is competitive. Ashgrove Partners tried to preempt in March with a term sheet at EUR 42M pre, and the founders held the process open specifically because they wanted a European deep-tech lead. We are the preferred lead at a lower price on the strength of our follow-on record. Sam Okafor at Halcyon has soft-circled EUR 2M as a co-investor and is doing his own confirmatory work this week; the remainder comes from existing angels.

6. Risks
(a) Packaging yield is still at 61% versus an 80% target — Rafael's roadmap gets there by Q1 2027, but slippage would push out gross margin targets. (b) Customer concentration: two pilots represent all revenue. (c) Ashgrove could re-engage aggressively if we stall; we should sign within two weeks.

7. Terms and process
Standard Series A docs, 1x non-participating preference, 10% option pool refresh pre-money. We propose instructing counsel immediately upon IC approval so we can move to signing by 30 April.

Ask: approval to issue a term sheet at EUR 38M pre for EUR 7M, board seat, pro-rata rights.

— Jonas

title: IC Memo — Copperleaf Freight Series A (PASS)
body:
NORDWIND VENTURES — INVESTMENT COMMITTEE MEMO

Company: Copperleaf Freight B.V. (Rotterdam)
Round: Series A — EUR 9M sought at EUR 30M pre-money
Prepared by: Jonas Berg (Associate)
Reviewed by: Maya Chen (Partner)
Date: 22 June 2026

RECOMMENDATION: PASS

This memo records our reasoning for fund memory. The company is likely to raise regardless of our decision, and if the Series B comes back to us in 12-18 months we should be able to reconstruct exactly why we stepped away and what would need to be true for us to change our minds.

1. Summary
Copperleaf Freight operates a digital freight brokerage for short-sea shipping routes in Northern Europe, matching cargo owners with underutilised coaster vessels. The deal came to us via Theo Marchetti at CasselBlu, who has been advising the company on its raise. Founder Anouk Verhoeven (CEO), previously VP of network operations at Transverra Logistics, is genuinely impressive: deep operator knowledge, strong commercial instincts, and she has grown GMV to EUR 18M in under two years.

2. Why we are passing
(a) Margin structure. Net revenue is 6.2% of GMV and has declined each quarter as the company chases volume. Our expert call on 11 June with Gordon Marsh, former COO of Transverra Logistics and Anouk's old boss, was the turning point: he argued persuasively that short-sea brokerage take rates compress toward 4-5% at scale because vessel operators disintermediate the platform once lanes become predictable. His call notes are filed in the diligence folder and worth rereading before any future look.
(b) Capital intensity. The plan requires EUR 25M+ of further funding before breakeven, which at these margins implies heavy dilution or a structurally difficult Series B.
(c) Churn masked by growth. Cohort data shows 38% of shippers from H1 2025 are inactive; new logo acquisition is hiding this.
(d) Price. EUR 30M pre for EUR 1.1M net revenue is a software multiple on a brokerage business.

3. What happened instead
Ashgrove Partners led the round at the full asking price, with Camille Fontaine taking the board seat. Camille called Maya after signing to ask whether we would join as a smaller co-investor; we declined for the reasons above. Notably, Ashgrove also outbid everyone on two other logistics deals this quarter — worth tracking their thesis, as we keep meeting them at the same tables (they were also the underbidder on Saltglass Photonics in April).

4. What would change our mind
For the Series B: net take rate stabilised above 6% for three consecutive quarters, shipper cohort retention above 75%, and evidence that vessel operators are not disintermediating the top ten lanes. If Anouk hits those numbers, this becomes a very different conversation and we should move quickly — the founder quality here is real.

5. Relationship handling
Jonas to send a candid, warm pass note to Anouk this week and keep a quarterly check-in. Theo has been told verbally; no bridges burned.

— Jonas
